message.content:
Lions (*Panthera leo*) and zebras (*Equus quagga*) belong to very different branches of the mammalian tree—lions are members of the order **Carnivora** (Felidae), while zebras are part of the order **Perissodactyla** (Equidae).  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore a small, early mammal that lived roughly **65 – 70 million years ago**, during the Paleocene epoch, before the split between the carnivore lineage and the perissodactyl lineage.  

This ancestor would have been a relatively simple, insect‑eating mammal that lived on the northern continents (Laurasia) and represents the last common ancestor of all modern placental mammals that later diversified into the wide array of forms we see today.
